title: LoRa-Based Multi-Hop Network for Smart Water Metering Devices
content: Smart water metering requires low-power, large-scale communication that existing LPWAN solutions do not fully address: the single-hop topology of LoRaWAN needs dense gateway deployments in urban environments, and cellular alternatives incur subscription costs and higher energy consumption. This paper presents a multi-hop LoRa protocol for smart water metering that exploits the static topology and uplink-dominated traffic of this application to simplify the protocol design. Each node selects its relay through a lightweight message exchange and a cost function that combines hop count, relay load and link quality, using only local information, so that the network forms a tree rooted at the gateway. Overhearing the relay retransmission replaces dedicated acknowledgement packets on the relayed hops. The cost function coefficients were tuned by Bayesian optimization for networks of up to 100 nodes, and the best configuration depends on network size. Compared with a shortest-hop (BFS) baseline, the mean peak relay load settles at about 12 clients for 40 to 100 nodes, a reduction of up to 71%, for an average hop-count increase of up to 13%. The transmit energy of the busiest relay falls by up to 69%, although its daily consumption remains dominated by reception. The evaluation covers the topology produced by relay selection and the resulting analytical energy budget.
